prompt: A 2 kg block of iron cools from 80 °C, giving out 36000 J of heat. What is its final temperature? The specific heat capacity of iron is 450 J/kg°C.
note: Q = mcΔT with Q = -36000 J: ΔT = -40 °C, so 80 - 40. Read as +36000 J it was 120 °C (review 2026-11-11)

prompt: A 2 kg block of iron cools to 40 °C, giving out 36000 J of heat. What was its initial temperature? (c = 450 J/kg°C)
note: 40 + 36000/(2 × 450); it was 0 °C with the sign dropped

prompt: A 2 kg block of iron at 20 °C absorbs 36000 J of heat. What is its final temperature? (c = 450 J/kg°C)
note: 20 + 36000/(2 × 450): the same law, its heat taken in

prompt: 2 mol of an ideal gas at 300 K is compressed isothermally from 10 L. 3000 J of work is done on the gas. What is the final volume?
note: W_by = nRT ln(V2/V1) = -3000 J: V2 = 10 × exp(-3000/(2 × 8.314 × 300)); 18.2 L with the sign dropped

prompt: A 2 kg ball moving at 5 m/s is hit by a bat with an average force of 40 N for 0.1 s in the opposite direction. What is its final speed?
note: v = u + Ft/m = 5 - 40 × 0.1/2; 7 m/s with the force's direction dropped

prompt: Two forces act on a box in opposite directions. The net force is 10 N and one force is 30 N. What is the other force?
note: 20 N or 40 N: the question does not say which way the 30 N acts

prompt: A lens forms an inverted image 4 cm tall with a magnification of -2. How tall is the object?
note: h_o = h_i/m = (-4)/(-2): the inverted image's height is negative

prompt: A wrench applies a torque of 30 newton metres to a bolt. The wrench is 0.5 m long. What force is applied?
note: F = τ/r = 30/0.5; "30 N metres" was a force of 30 N and a torque of 15 N·m

prompt: An impulse of 20 newton seconds acts on a 4 kg cart for 2 s. What is the average force?
A bat delivers an impulse of 6 newton-seconds over 0.3 s. What is the change in momentum of the ball?
note: Δp = J; 1.8 N·s with the second word dropped

prompt: A car of mass 1 200 kg moves at 20 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
note: ½ × 1200 × 20²; read as 200 kg it was 40 000 J

prompt: A \(1\,500\,\text{kg}\) car accelerates at \(2\,\text{m/s}^2\). What is the net force?
note: 1500 × 2; a thin space between digit groups

prompt: A car of mass \(1\,500\,\text{kg}\) has a kinetic energy of \(300\,\text{kJ}\). What is its speed?
A 6 kg block is cut in half. What is the weight of each half?
note: 3 kg × 9.81; the whole block's 58.9 N is not a half's

prompt: An object has a density of 2 g/cm³ and a volume of 3 cm³ and is cut in half. What is the mass of each half?
note: 2 × 3/2; the whole's 6 g is not a half's

prompt: A 6 kg block is split into three equal pieces. What is the weight of each piece?
Two identical 3 kg blocks sit on a table. What is the weight of each block?
note: each block is 3 kg: 3 × 9.81

prompt: Two charges q1 = 2 μC and q2 = 3 μC are 0.3 m apart, with k = 9 × 10^9 N·m²/C². Find the force.
note: 9e9 × 6e-12/0.09 with the stated k, not CODATA's 8.99e9 (0.599 N)

prompt: Two point charges of \(2\,\mu\text{C}\) and \(3\,\mu\text{C}\) are \(0.3\,\text{m}\) apart. What is the electrostatic force between them? (Use \(F = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{q_1q_2}{r^2}\).)
note: 8.99e9 × 6e-12/0.09; the constant written 1/(4πε₀)

prompt: The critical angle of glass is 42°. Calculate the refractive index of glass.
note: n = 1/sin 42° = 1.494; solved backwards from 42° in radians read as degrees it was 78.2 (review 2026-11-11). Main declines it too.

prompt: The critical angle for diamond is 24.4°. What is the refractive index of diamond?
note: n = 2.42; it was 135

Light falls on a grating with 300 lines per mm. The first-order maximum is at an angle of 10.4°. What is the wavelength?
